title: Runner-Neutral Verification and Admission Checkpoint Architecture

preflight.note: Recorded before RepoPact implementation work began. Triggered by the 2026-09-01 ForgeWire local-only validation transition after GitHub-hosted execution became unavailable, and by WI039's completed enforcement-closure field study. This item is architecture/reconciliation-first and does not pre-authorize a specific schema or provider integration.

acceptance_criteria.text: A durable field-evidence capture characterizes at least two distinct real enforcement-closure failures already observed in the ForgeWire Labs ecosystem: a governed CI path that existed but did not invoke RepoPact, and a hosted checkpoint that could not execute because the provider/account was unavailable while equivalent local execution remained possible. The capture separates checkpoint definition, execution venue, invocation, effectiveness, and admission enforcement rather than treating 'CI' as one boolean property.

The proposed verification/checkpoint abstraction is formally reconciled with WI039 and the existing enforcement-closure model (checkpoint coverage, invocation, effectiveness / Cov, Inv, Eff). The work states which concepts are new versus already represented, preserves the admission-boundary definition, and does not retroactively rewrite completed field evidence.

An architecture decision establishes the boundary that RepoPact owns the verification/admission contract and its evidence semantics, while execution venues remain replaceable adapters. RepoPact must not become a hosted CI service, worker scheduler, container fleet manager, or remote execution fabric; those responsibilities remain with GitHub/GitLab/AppVeyor/Jenkins/operator-owned runners/ForgeWire Fabric or equivalent executors.

Before schema implementation, at least four candidate record placements are evaluated for checkpoint definition and execution policy: governance policy/front matter, a dedicated checkpoint/verification record, extensions to work-item acceptance criteria, and extensions to evidence-run records (or an explicitly justified equivalent set). The chosen design explains source-of-truth, lifecycle, reference semantics, derivation boundaries, and migration behavior.

The chosen model can define runner-neutral verification profiles or equivalent named contracts that specify what is checked, the governed admission boundary, required capabilities/platforms, failure semantics, and evidence expectations independently of where execution occurs. Local workstation, hosted CI, self-hosted runner, and remote Fabric-style execution can invoke the same logical contract without duplicating its command semantics in provider YAML.

Local execution is designed and tested as a first-class reference path rather than a degraded afterthought. A provider outage can therefore be represented truthfully as hosted invocation unavailable while local verification remains executable; the model does not falsely claim remote admission enforcement when only local evidence exists.

Execution-venue policy can express operator-controlled restrictions such as local-only mode, hosted execution disabled, or an allowlist of acceptable executor classes without coupling RepoPact to provider billing APIs. Hosted execution must never be silently enabled merely because a workflow file exists; changing an operator-declared execution policy follows normal RepoPact authority/frozen-surface rules.

Evidence produced by checkpoint execution is repository-native and venue-neutral. The design records enough identity to establish the checkpoint/profile, candidate commit or tree, executor/venue class, environment/capabilities, commands/checks, result, and artifacts while preserving existing concrete/provisional/inferred provenance semantics. The work explicitly decides whether this is an additive evidence-run extension or a referenced companion record.

The work defines how admission enforcement is represented separately from successful verification. At minimum it can distinguish a passing local run with no merge gate, a hosted gate that exists but is unavailable, a checker that runs but whose failure is ignored, and a closed admission boundary where every governed path invokes the applicable checker and failure prevents promotion.

RepoPact adopt/doctor behavior is reconciled with the new abstraction. Existing .github/workflows discovery must no longer imply that GitHub workflow identity itself is the universal gate model: adoption may infer checkpoint contracts and venue adapters with honest inferred/provisional provenance, and doctor provides a non-destructive migration/ratchet path for repositories previously represented only by binding-gate workflow policies.

Provider adapters are thin and mechanically checkable. At least a local runner and GitHub Actions adapter are demonstrated against the same logical verification contract; the architecture also proves that an operator-owned/self-hosted or ForgeWire-style executor can consume that contract without introducing RepoPact-to-Fabric coupling. A reusable GitHub Action, if shipped, is an adapter derived from this architecture rather than the canonical definition of the gate.

Derived RepoPact views expose checkpoint state without overclaiming it. Dashboard/spec/reporting can distinguish declared coverage, demonstrated invocation, demonstrated effectiveness, executor availability, and enforcement closure at relevant admission boundaries; stale or provider-unavailable state is visible instead of being collapsed into a generic CI pass/fail label.

Conformance/regression coverage contains positive and negative cases for at least: same verification contract executed locally and through a hosted adapter; workflow present but applicable checker absent; checker configured but unavailable; checker failure ignored; closed admission gate rejecting an invalid candidate; hosted venue disabled by operator policy while local execution succeeds; and evidence from one venue incorrectly claimed as proof of another venue's enforcement.

The architecture is validated against the real ForgeWire local-only transition and at least one adopter-neutral synthetic or public-repository fixture. Closeout evidence explains what would falsify the claim that the contract is runner-neutral rather than overfit to GitHub Actions or ForgeWire.

Backward compatibility and versioning are decided before implementation lands. Existing RepoPact repositories and historical evidence remain valid unless an explicit breaking-version decision is accepted; current WI032 remote-enforcement work is reconciled rather than silently superseded, with remote/public checkpoint restoration remaining a separate operational concern from the generic runner-neutral checkpoint architecture.

After the architecture and compatibility decisions are accepted, the selected model is implemented consistently across all required schema, validator, CLI, templates, adopt/doctor, SPEC, documentation, dashboard, conformance, and test surfaces. Derived artifacts are regenerated from sources, frozen-surface changes follow operator approval, and closeout includes a negative enforcement proof rather than only green-path tests.
